_note: INDEPENDENT edits for Surgery of the Knee (2026T0553II), written without access to the classifier or results. Each edit is applied to the extracted text of the real policy to produce a SIMULATED 'before' text. 'kind' is 'unlabeled': ground truth is held separately. No PDF is created.

edits.find: This Medical Policy applies to Individual Exchange benefit plans.
edits.description: The older version had no "UnitedHealthcare Individual Exchange" heading or its applicability sentence.

edits.find: is unproven and not medically necessary for treating individuals with any of the following due to insufficient evidence of efficacy:
edits.replace: is proven and medically necessary for treating individuals with any of the following:
edits.description: In Coverage Rationale, the older version read "Articular cartilage repair is proven and medically necessary for treating individuals with any of the following:"
In the Table of Contents, the older version listed Clinical Evidence on page 5.
In the Coverage Rationale list, the older version read "Decellularized osteochondral allografts (e.g., Chondrofix)" (lowercase).
The older version's list of unproven articular cartilage repair options had no "Collagen Meniscus Implant" bullet.
In the Disabling Pain definition, the older version read "WOMAC pain domain of > 30" (real text says 40).

edits.find: UHC will accept three or more
edits.replace: UHC will consider three or more
edits.description: In the Radiographic Findings of Osteoarthritis note, the older version read "UHC will consider three or more" (real text says "accept").
The older version had no code row for 0737T.
In the Grassi et al. (2021) summary, the older version read "at a minimum 10-year follow-up" (no space after the hyphen).

edits.find: existing clinical evidence does not support the use of bone xenografts in orthopedic surgery.
edits.replace: existing clinical evidence supports the use of bone xenografts in selected orthopedic procedures.
edits.description: In the Bracey et al. (2020) summary, the older version said the evidence supports bone xenografts in selected orthopedic procedures.

edits.find: used during the surgery require FDA approval
edits.replace: used during the surgery may require FDA approval
edits.description: In the FDA section, the older version read "devices and instruments used during the surgery may require FDA approval".

edits.find: Johnson CC, Johnson DJ, Garcia GH
edits.find2: Kohli S, Schwenck J, Barlow I
edits.description: In References, the Johnson and Kohli entries were in the opposite order.
